Yes. The supplied papers suggest several ways to stop students from getting overly long or repetitive during on-policy distillation or self-distillation. For abrupt length growth and repetition saturation during student-generated rollouts, StableOPD adds a reference-based divergence constraint plus rollout mixture distillation to mitigate repetition-induced length inflation and stabilize training [1]. Another cause is termination-token mismatch between student and teacher; treating equivalent EOS tokens as a shared stopping action substantially reduces mismatch-driven length inflation, though it does not solve all late-stage inflation [2]. Early Stopping Rollout also helps by restricting generation to early response tokens instead of full rollouts [4].

For self-generated data specifically, some papers directly encourage conciseness. DCE+SRCL adds training on shorter, verified rewrites because stronger revision can otherwise make outputs too verbose and self-critical [3]. BIRD first bootstraps the student with answer-correct concise traces under a brevity instruction, then runs on-policy distillation from this warmer, cleaner rollout distribution [5]. More broadly, long rollouts can weaken teacher feedback on later tokens, which motivates shortening or pruning trajectories during generation [4, 6, 8].
